subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a surface-trained illusionist who has performed a con involving a spider and Dancing Lights to impersonate a vessel of Lolth, successfully manipulating Asha Vandree by reframing his deception as a divine test she passed.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a paranoid, fanatically devoted follower of Lolth who believes Ilvara is corrupted by Zuggtmoy’s spores, and who misinterpreted Daz’s illusion as a divine trial — ultimately revealing critical intelligence about Ilvara’s operations while remaining terrified of contamination.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube acting as a familiar who failed to remain inert during a critical negotiation, speaking and moving in ways that threatened the illusion — yet was dismissed by Asha as eccentricity of a spore-addled convert.
source_quote: Glabbagool, I'm taking care of this, it's fine.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow who observed the entire negotiation in silence, treated as invisible by Asha Vandree, and used his drow-trained patience to gather intelligence, noting tactical details and emotional undercurrents without drawing attention.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a spellcaster who presented three powerful 4th-level spells — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer — but revealed he can only cast one due to limited spell slots, forcing the group to prioritize their approach to assassinating Ilvara.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become obsessed with the idea of Lolth being married, and now leads a fungal cult that transforms followers into mindless fungal creatures using spores, posing a spreading threat to the Underdark.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married... all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Lolth's Followers
fact: Among Asha Vandree’s sect, true devotion to Lolth is defined by rigid, fear-based orthodoxy — rejecting any display of emotion or uncertainty as false, and viewing spiritual possession or fungal corruption as heresy or infection.
source_quote: That is not the kind of conviction a follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Zuggtmoy's Spores
fact: The spores of Zuggtmoy are a fungal infection capable of inducing madness, delusions of divine connection, and physical transformation, and are feared as a contagious, mind-corrupting force in the Underdark.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy?

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a powerful magical artifact associated with Ilvara’s cult, not itself the vector of infection but a dangerous relic that must be destroyed to prevent its power from spreading.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: Negotiation with Asha Vandree
fact: A negotiation occurred in which Daz’s illusion of Lolth’s possession was misinterpreted by Asha as a divine test of her discernment, leading her to reveal critical intelligence about Ilvara’s cult, spores, and the Heart Fungus, while remaining terrified of contamination.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Assassination Planning
fact: The party planned the assassination of Ilvara using Grygum’s limited 4th-level spell slots, debating whether to use Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, or Phantasmal Killer — each offering a different tactical advantage against a paranoid, fungal-corrupted target.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: Underdark Cavern
fact: The cavern is a fungal-infested Underdark chamber where Asha has been isolated for an extended period, monitoring Ilvara’s cult, and where the party conducted their negotiation and planned their assault, with hidden zones of darkness prepared for retreat.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman is a 4th-level spell that creates a 20-foot sphere dealing 20 points of damage per turn to all creatures within, usable from 120 feet away, and considered for use in the assassination of Ilvara.
source_quote: It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Phantasmal Killer
fact: Phantasmal Killer is a 4th-level spell that taps into a creature’s deepest fears, creating an illusory manifestation that can cause up to 4d10 psychic damage per turn if the target fails consecutive Wisdom saves, and was considered for use against Ilvara’s corrupted mind.
source_quote: It says you tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see and create an illusory manifestation of its deepest fears... then they take 4 die 10 psychic damage.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: Glyph of Warding is a 4th-level spell that can be inscribed on a surface or object and triggered by movement or action, used in planning to ambush Ilvara without direct confrontation.
source_quote: You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Zalthir’s Invisibility
fact: Zalthir’s complete erasure from Asha Vandree’s perception during the negotiation remains an unresolved thread — whether her bias against drow is cultural, personal, or magical — and whether he will later exploit this invisibility in the assault.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward.

subject: Glabbagool’s Sentience
fact: Glabbagool’s unexpected speech and movement during the negotiation suggest he may possess latent intelligence or be influenced by fungal spores — a mystery the party has noted but not yet addressed.
source_quote: The cube subsided. I did not visibly react. Somewhere behind my eyes, I filed it away in the archive of things I have witnessed that I will never be able to explain.

subject: session date
fact: The events of this chapter occur during a single session of play, with the negotiation, planning, and preparation unfolding in real-time before the planned assault on Ilvara.
source_quote: I spent the hour before the assault doing the thing that was useful and quiet and required no discussion.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is planning the assassination of Ilvara, having deferred to Asha's tactical expertise despite her contempt, and has internalized critical intelligence about the Heart Fungus as infrastructure rather than a mere target.
source_quote: I took the note. I filed it. I did not say anything I would regret.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow priestess of Lolth who holds tactical authority over the operation against Ilvara, dismissive of Grygum but correct about the Heart Fungus being the key to dismantling Ilvara’s power structure.
source_quote: I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the party who raised concerns about spore contamination and proposed the final tactical sequence involving grappling Ilvara into the Phantasmal Killer spell.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Dragonborn who has been infected by Ilvara's spores, serving as a visual warning to the party, and is credited with securing Glabbagool as an ooze familiar, earning Asha’s reluctant respect.
source_quote: Look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a former lover of Ilvara, now bitter and estranged, whose emotional vulnerability was exploited by Thorin to trigger the Glyph of Warding on the bridge.
source_quote: Jorlan still is complaining that Ilvara… Ilvara this and Ilvara that.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who adapted to the ranged nature of the battle by accepting a crossbow and manipulated Jorlan’s rage to activate the Glyph of Warding, turning emotional history into tactical advantage.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara’s cult consists of drow who have embraced her heretical claims that she is Lolth’s further manifestation, and have willingly succumbed to her spores, becoming hollowed-out spore servants.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Lolth's Faithful
fact: Lolth’s faithful, represented by Asha, reject Ilvara’s heresy and maintain strict devotion to the Spider Queen, distinguishing themselves from those corrupted by the bride cult.
source_quote: I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy.

subject: activation of the Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding inscribed on the bridge was triggered by Jorlan’s charge, killing one spore servant and severely damaging another, while also shuddering the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: The detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing...

subject: Zalthir's teleport and grapple on Ilvara
fact: Zalthir teleported to Ilvara and successfully grappled her, initiating the final phase of the assassination plan by attempting to drop her into the Phantasmal Killer spell.
source_quote: Zalthir vanish — just gone, teleported straight to her — and then there's the crack of his fists finding purchase...

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a massive, pulsing fungal entity at the center of Ilvara’s domain, serving as the structural anchor of her control over the cavern and its spore servants.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus pulsed between us and her, enormous and obscene, the mechanism of her control.

subject: Bridge of the Glyph
fact: The bridge is a strategic chokepoint where Grygum inscribed a Glyph of Warding keyed to Jorlan’s approach, turning the structure into a lethal threshold for Ilvara’s allies.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a magical substance originally intended for direct use against Ilvara, but reclassified by Asha as superior for infrastructure demolition — specifically, to destroy the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman... was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is a rune inscribed by Grygum on the bridge, designed to detonate upon approach from Jorlan’s side, functioning as a trap keyed to emotional history rather than factional loyalty.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze creature presented as Daz’s familiar, whose unnatural presence impressed Asha and provided a cover story to avoid suspicion during the infiltration.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are former drow guards who have fully succumbed to Ilvara’s spores, now shambling, corrupted husks bound to her will and acting as frontline enforcers.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong...

subject: Asha's lingering doubt
fact: Asha’s final statement — 'I believe' — introduces critical uncertainty into her otherwise authoritative intelligence, suggesting her knowledge of Ilvara’s spores may be incomplete or faith-based rather than empirical.
source_quote: I believe.

subject: Jorlan and Ilvara's broken romance
fact: The unresolved romantic history between Jorlan and Ilvara is a destabilizing emotional undercurrent that influences factional loyalty and was weaponized tactically by Thorin.
source_quote: They used to have an affair... she broke up with him, and then he was bitter...

subject: Grygum's loss of Asha's respect
fact: Asha refuses to speak directly to Grygum, indicating he has lost her trust, creating a silent rift that may hinder coordination during execution.
source_quote: She delivered the actual intelligence — through Daz, not through me, because I had apparently lost her respect...

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during the planning and execution of the assassination of Ilvara, following the party's arrival in the Underdark and their prior visit to the Whorlstone Caverns.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension...

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me, because of course it does, and the first swing misses clean — the thing reaches up and just swings into nothing, which is the best that can be said about it — but the second one connects. Five damage. A glancing thing. Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard, flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise. The thing shudders. Good. Let it shudder.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.
source_quote: And then Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is bleeding. The mushroom icon she carries is smoldering after taking 24 damage from a Fireball.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is still in front of Thorin.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is still in Thorin's hand.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: mushroom icon
fact: The mushroom icon carried by Ilvara is smoldering after taking 24 damage from a Fireball.
source_quote: And then Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: Fireball impact
fact: A Fireball centered on Ilvara and her mushroom icon deals 24 damage despite her saving throw.
source_quote: And then Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: spore walker attack
fact: A spore walker attacks Thorin, missing the first swing but connecting on the second for five damage.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me, because of course it does, and the first swing misses clean — the thing reaches up and just swings into nothing, which is the best that can be said about it — but the second one connects. Five damage. A glancing thing.

subject: Heart Fungus grinding
fact: Grygum grinds the Heart Fungus, delivering twenty force damage per turn, causing it to shudder.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise. The thing shudders. Good. Let it shudder.

subject: mushroom icon's fate
fact: The mushroom icon is smoldering and Ilvara is bleeding — its survival or restoration is uncertain.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.
